papers.title: Structural basis of the transport mechanism of hBGT1.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of the betaine/GABA transporter 1 (BGT1) reveal how it recognizes two chemically distinct substrates—GABA and betaine—and transitions between occluded and inward-open states. A proposed Na3-binding site limits reverse transport and promotes substrate accumulation, clarifying ion-coupling mechanisms shared with other neurotransmitter transporters.

papers.title: Contextual control of CD8(+) T cell priming by dendritic cell subsets in tumor and inflammatory microenvironments.
papers.summary: Using fluorescent antigen tracking across tumor, inflamed, and steady-state tissues, this study shows migratory type 1 dendritic cells outperform lymph node-resident counterparts in cross-presentation and CD8+ T cell priming. Antigen access plus subset-specific cross-presentation efficiency together predict priming quality, supporting strategies that augment resident dendritic cell cross-presentation.

papers.title: S1P mimics phosphorylation to mediate PDK1-independent activation of aPKC with an opposing downstream effect.
papers.summary: Sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) and PDK1 activate atypical PKC isoforms through a mutually exclusive, shared switch: the S1P phosphate occupies the same position as the phosphorylated activation-loop threonine. S1P-driven basal aPKC signaling suppresses apoptosis, whereas PDK1 phosphorylation promotes it—positioning aPKC at a lipid-versus-kinase signaling crossroads.

papers.title: Energetic dysregulations in psychotic disorders: Targets for new therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence for brain- and body-wide energetic dysregulation in psychotic disorders, spanning genetics, cellular models, postmortem tissue, and neuroimaging. Mitochondrial and redox abnormalities, central insulin resistance, and antipsychotic effects on metabolism converge on candidate therapeutic targets, with existing metabolic treatments proposed as a framework for new interventions.

papers.title: On the evolution of Neurospora crassa ACW-1 and NCW-3, proteins with different cell wall interaction mechanisms.
papers.summary: In Neurospora crassa, the cell wall proteins ACW-1 (GPI-anchored) and NCW-3 (CBM-52 domain) both bind β-1,3-glucans and localize to septa and hyphal walls. Despite similar global conservation and purifying selection, only ACW-1 shows a divergence gradient across its leucine-rich repeats, showing distinct architectures diversify differently.

papers.title: Sclerostin regulates bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) bioavailability through interactions with BMP complexes and fibrillin microfibrils.
papers.summary: Sclerostin (SOST) binds fibrillin-1/2 microfibrils via their N-terminal FUN domains and also engages BMP-7 and BMP-10 prodomains and complexes. Fibrillin-bound SOST occludes the BMP prodomain targeting site, establishing SOST as an extracellular-matrix-associated modulator linking microfibril scaffolds to fine-tuning of BMP and WNT signaling.

papers.title: Wdr5 Modulates Synaptic Development and Memory Consolidation in the Hippocampus and Cerebral Cortex.
papers.summary: Postnatal deletion of Wdr5, a core SET1/MLL histone methyltransferase component, in excitatory forebrain neurons impairs learning and memory in mice, with defective dendritic spine and synapse development in cortex and hippocampus. Dysregulated fear-conditioning gene responses—including Notch and mitochondrial respiratory pathways—identify WDR5 as critical for memory consolidation.

papers.title: Effects of elemental-based formulation on grain trace elements, amino acid profiles, antioxidant enzyme activities, gene expression and arsenic uptake in soil-grown rice under arsenic stress.
papers.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
papers.summary: A selenium-containing elemental-based formulation (EBF) alleviated arsenic stress in soil-grown rice: treated plants recovered 29–37% more critical minerals (Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu), showed up to 32% higher antioxidant enzyme activity, and altered amino acid and stress-gene expression. EBF offers a practical route to reduce grain arsenic accumulation in affected regions.

papers.title: Planarian progenitor responses to injury are not specific to missing tissue identity.
papers.summary: Planarian stem-cell responses to injury are not tailored to which tissue is missing. Even injuries sparing mature tissue increased progenitor incorporation into brain, nerve cord, and pharynx; epidermal regeneration relied on post-mitotic progenitors. Regeneration specificity instead reflects ongoing turnover, wound-driven division, and spatially broad specification zones.

papers.title: Postnatal heart development is coordinated by multi-lineage Wnt and BMP signaling.
papers.summary: Neonatal mouse hearts transition from cardiomyocyte proliferation to enlargement and binucleation between postnatal days 3.5–4.5, accompanied by declining β-catenin and rising SMAD1/5/9 phosphorylation. Wnt components act across endothelial, mesenchymal, and neural lineages while BMP peaks in cardiomyocytes later, revealing multi-lineage Wnt–BMP coordination of heart growth.

papers.title: Glycan-mediated interactions of infectious hypodermal and hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHHNV) with host tissues in Pacific whiteleg shrimp (Penaeus vannamei).
papers.summary: Virus-like particles of IHHNV, a shrimp pathogen, bind preferentially to muscle and gill tissues rich in oligomannosylated N-glycans and unusually substituted fucosylated O-glycans. Lectin and glycosidase blocking assays show mannosylated and fucosylated glycans are essential for viral recognition, suggesting conserved glycan motifs as broad-spectrum antiviral targets in aquaculture.

papers.title: Protein O-Mannosyltransferases in development and disease: evolutionary and functional insights from model organisms.
papers.summary: This review examines protein O-mannosyltransferases POMT1/2, which initiate α-dystroglycan O-mannosylation, through Drosophila and zebrafish models. It highlights dystroglycan-independent substrates—including receptor protein tyrosine phosphatases in neural circuit formation—and compensatory mechanisms underlying dystroglycanopathies, offering a tiered experimental framework linking simplified glycans, genetics, and conserved disease mechanisms.

papers.title: The protein sequence modulates terminal GalNAc incorporation during N-glycan biosynthesis.
papers.summary: Using isotope-assisted NMR on SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD expressed in HEK293F cells, mutating four solvent-exposed basic residues near N-glycosylation sites markedly reduced terminal GalNAc epitopes (including LacdiNAc forms) and increased galactose-containing structures, without altering protein fold—direct evidence that local protein sequence modulates Golgi glycan processing.

papers.title: Pumilio and Brain tumor regulate the expression of Smaug during the Drosophila maternal-to-zygotic transition.
papers.summary: During the Drosophila maternal-to-zygotic transition, the RNA-binding protein Pumilio promotes Smaug mRNA degradation through cis-elements in its 3′ UTR, with Brain tumor also repressing ectopic Smaug. Loss of either causes ectopic Smaug protein that broadly downregulates Smaug-target mRNAs, defining a pathway ensuring orderly MZT progression.

papers.title: Mutational bias and local genome context constrain adaptive paths in experimental evolution.
papers.summary: In 95 parallel yeast chemostat evolution replicates across glucose, phosphate, and sulfate limitation, whole-genome sequencing revealed recurrent targets including SAGA in sulfate limitation, sirtuins in phosphate limitation, and the phosphorelay system in glucose limitation. Ty1/Ty2 mobilizations preferentially interrupted genes whose genome context predicts transposon targeting, constraining adaptive paths.

papers.title: Krüppel-like factors regulate lipid homeostasis to modulate SKN-1/Nrf activity, oxidative stress resistance and longevity.
papers.summary: In C. elegans, the Krüppel-like factor KLF-1 modulates SKN-1A/NRF1 and SKN-1C/NRF2 activity through lipid homeostasis, influencing oxidative stress resistance and germline-deficient longevity without changing SKN-1 transcripts. KLF-1 and KLF-2 oppositely regulate lipid accumulation and lipophagy genes, positioning KLF-dependent lipid regulation upstream of SKN-1 activation.

papers.title: Cooperative definition of ER exit sites by Tango1, Sec16 and Sec12.
papers.summary: In Drosophila, Sec16 and Tango1 are interdependent for endoplasmic reticulum exit site (ERES) assembly, with CG9175 identified as the Sec12 ortholog required upstream for coordinating Tango1 and Sec16 concentration. Both Tango1 and Sec16 concentrate COPII and COPI components, defining a cooperative three-protein network for animal ERES.

papers.title: Identifying patterns of selection at synonymous sites in a Pseudomonas phylogeny.
papers.summary: Bayesian stochastic character mapping across Pseudomonas gtsb and gtsd identifies four-fold degenerate synonymous sites under constraint: 8% and 7.5% show substitution rates and patterns comparable to nonsynonymous positions, including experimentally verified beneficial sites. Neither codon usage, structure, nor sequence motifs explain this variation, suggesting non-neutral synonymous mutations frequently contribute to adaptation.

papers.title: FABP5 regulates an immunosuppressive microenvironment in hepatocellular carcinoma through the NF-κB/PD-L1 axis.
papers.summary: FABP5 is upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma and predicts worse survival, expressed mainly in fibroblasts and macrophages. Knockdown suppressed proliferation and EMT markers; mechanistically FABP5 drives PD-L1 upregulation via NF-κB, creating an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Drug screening identified CZS-241 as a stable FABP5-binding candidate with therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Network of interactions between the tumor necrosis factor superfamily members and small S100 proteins.
papers.summary: Surface plasmon resonance mapping revealed 27 calcium-dependent interactions between 13 soluble TNF superfamily ligands—including CD70, 4-1BBL, and APRIL—and S100 calcium-binding proteins, with affinities from 2 nM to 24 μM. Conserved docking sites and S100P 'hinge' mutagenesis expose a regulatory interaction network potentially exploitable for targeted therapy.

papers.title: Vaping during pregnancy and maternal, fetal, and infant health outcomes: A scoping review of human and animal studies.
papers.summary: This scoping review of 64 studies (30 human, 34 animal) finds pregnancy vaping evidence too heterogeneous for firm risk conclusions. Human studies are mostly observational with unvalidated self-reported exposure; animal studies suggest metabolic, respiratory, cardiovascular, and neurobehavioural effects, highlighting the need for prospective studies with objective exposure assessment.

papers.title: Heterotrimeric G proteins containing Gβ1γ2 subunits exhibit subtype-specific mobility differences in live cells.
papers.summary: Single-molecule imaging in live cells shows heterotrimeric G proteins containing Gβ1γ2 differ markedly in membrane mobility depending on their Gα subunit: Gα12/Gα13-containing heterotrimers move far less than Gαi/o or Gαs types. Subtype-specific lateral mobility is thus a factor shaping GPCR signaling dynamics in living cells.

papers.title: Tumor specific cytokine pattern explored in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.summary: Antibody arrays across 20 early-stage renal cell carcinoma tissue sets identified 34 differentially expressed cytokines, enriched in TNF, PI3K-AKT, and HIF-1 pathways. ELISA confirmed reduced IL-2, IL-15, IGFBP-2, HGF, ERBB3, and FLT3LG with elevated CCL4, CXCL9, and angiopoietin-2; urinary ERBB3 emerged as a candidate non-invasive biomarker.

papers.title: Genome wide identification and analysis of inositol tetrakisphosphate kinase (ITPK) gene family in Triticum aestivum L.
papers.summary: A genome-wide survey identified 15 inositol tetrakisphosphate kinase (ITPK) genes across bread wheat's A, B, and D subgenomes, spanning four phylogenetic groups with conserved kinase domains. Preferential post-anthesis expression and responses to iron and zinc supplementation provide a foundation for functional studies of phytic acid and mineral bioavailability.

papers.title: Role of Macrophages in Epimorphic Tissue Regeneration.
papers.summary: This review summarizes macrophage roles in epimorphic regeneration beyond zebrafish—salamander limb and lens, lizard tail, rodent fingertip and ear. Tissue-resident macrophages, largely established during embryogenesis, promote re-epithelialization, blastema formation, and matrix remodeling, with environment-dependent phenotypes distinguishing regenerative from inflammatory contributions across vertebrate models.

papers.title: Sequestosome 1 (SQSTM1/p62) at the nexus of genome integrity maintenance, proteostasis regulation and organellar homeostasis.
papers.summary: This review positions SQSTM1/p62—best known as a selective autophagy scaffold—at the intersection of proteostasis regulation, genome integrity maintenance, and organellar homeostasis. Integrating its roles in ubiquitin-proteasome crosstalk, endo/exosomal trafficking, and oxidative stress signaling, the authors frame open questions on p62 bridging these themes over the next decade.

papers.title: Steered molecular dynamics and free-energy analysis of withanolide unbinding from tau kinases TTBK1 and GSK-3β.
papers.summary: Steered molecular dynamics and umbrella sampling quantify withanolide binding to the tau kinases TTBK1 and GSK-3β, with calculated free energies of −9 to −13 kcal/mol and van der Waals contacts dominating complex stabilization. Ashwagandha-derived scaffolds emerge as promising starting points for structure-guided design of tau-directed therapeutics.

papers.title: Intrinsic endonucleolytic activity of snake venom phosphodiesterase.
papers.summary: Tracking nuclease activity through chromatography and LC-MS/MS, the authors show purified Naja atra snake venom phosphodiesterase converts closed circular plasmid DNA to linear forms and cleaves complementary strands at defined nicks—establishing endonucleolytic activity as intrinsic to this ENPP-family enzyme, with DNA topology influencing cleavage.

papers.title: Rapid and reliable molecular diagnosis of oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy: a cost-effective alternative for PABPN1 gene (GCN)n repeat analysis.
papers.summary: Capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis on 90 genomic DNA samples showed full concordance with Sanger sequencing for detecting expanded PABPN1 (GCN)n alleles causing oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy. Faster, simpler, and cheaper—avoiding fluorescent primers and costly instruments—it offers a practical diagnostic alternative for resource-limited laboratories.

papers.title: Severe neurodevelopmental phenotype with multisystem involvement in VPS16-related mucopolysaccharidosis-like syndrome.
papers.summary: A new patient with biallelic VPS16 variants showed profound developmental delay, early-onset epilepsy, spasticity, and multisystem features including neutropenia, serosal effusions, and tubular proteinuria. Brain MRI revealed progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with basal ganglia iron deposition, substantially expanding the neurological spectrum of this rare mucopolysaccharidosis-like syndrome.
